newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION PANKRATOV OUT IN HEATS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION PANKRATOV OUT IN HEATS.

text.p: Olympic champion Denis Pankratov failed to make the final of the men's 100 metres butterfly on the opening day of the world short-course swimming championships on Thursday.
The Russian world record-holder never reached his customary stride, trailing from the outset of the last heat behind team mate Konstantin Ushkov, who set a fast pace.
Ushkov led at the 50-metre mark in 24.22 seconds, with Pankratov a remote fifth in 25.04.
Pankratov, who won the 100 and 200 metres butterfly golds at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, could do nothing to cut back the deficit and finished more than a second behind Swedish winner Lars Frolander.
Frolander, out of Pankratov's immediate vision in the outside lane one, clocked a championship record 52.10 to win ahead of Australia's Geoff Huegill (52.69) and Canada's Garret Pulle (53.17).

Ushkov, who briefly held the European record this year before Pankratov broke it, paid for his fast opening pace and faded to fourth in 53.34 with Pankratov fifth in 53.48, way outside the 51.78 world mark he set in Paris in February.
The Russians finished 10th and 11th overall, both failing to make the evening's eight-strong final in the custom-built 25-metre tank in the Scandinavium indoor arena.
A resigned Pankratov, who came to Sweden from training camps in France which included a period at high altitude in the Pyrenees, did not want to talk about his disappointing showing.
He was sporting stubble on his chin and sources close to the team said he had been confident of qualifying and had not shaved down for the heats.
Fellow Olympic champion Le Jingyi of China made sure she did not suffer a similar fate in the women's 100 metres freestyle but managed only the third-fastest qualifying time.
Le, who won the 50 and 100 metres freestyle at both previous world short-course championships in 1993 and 1995, won her heat in 54.54, nowhere near her world record 53.01.

American Jenny Thompson, a relay gold medallist in Atlanta, clocked the fastest time of 53.94, appreciably swifter than Le, who said recently that these championships would serve as a warm-up for China's National Games in October.
Germany's Sandra Voelker, who missed Le's world mark by just 0.03 of a second at the European short-course championships in Rostock last December, was second-quickest in 53.96.
American Misty Hyman led the way in the women's 200 metres butterfly heats, claiming comfortably the fastest time of two minutes 7.78 seconds.
China's Qu Yun and Liu Limin, respectively fourth and fifth at the Atlanta Games, both made the final.
Qu was second overall in 2:09.34 and Liu, reigning world short-course 100 butterfly champion and silver medallist in the 200 event last time, seventh in 2:11.14.
Brazil's Gustavo Borges made a confident start to the defence of his 200 metres freestyle title, leading qualifiers in 1:46.94.
Australia's Matthew Dunn, double gold medallist at the last world short-course championships, led the way in his 400 individual medley title defence in 4:11.98.
Germany's Sabine Herbst was fastest qualifier in the women's 400 individual medley (4:39.18), slightly quicker than Canadian defending champion Joanne Malar (4:39.73).
